hints.title: Multiplicity Count Tracking
hints.text: Each number should appear in the intersection as many times as it appears in both input arrays. How can tracking frequencies preserve duplicate counts?

hints.title: Inventory Decrement Invariant
hints.text: Recording the frequency of numbers from the smaller array allows decrementing available stock as each matching value is encountered in the second array.

hints.title: Frequency Counter Matching Procedure
hints.text: Build a frequency count mapping from the first array. Iterate through each number in the second array. If the number exists in the mapping with a count greater than zero, add it to the result and decrement its count. Return the collected result.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N + M) time and O(min(N, M)) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Searching and removing items directly from array lists incurs quadratic O(N * M) deletion overhead.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Counting frequencies of the smaller array takes O(min(N, M)) space and processes both arrays in linear O(N + M) time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should discuss follow-ups: what if inputs are sorted (two-pointer), what if nums1 is much smaller than nums2, or memory is limited.
